chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
He heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: I advise you, O servants of Allah, to have God-consciousness.
And do not burden people with your weight (or expectations) so that you will be humiliated.
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says in His Book: Speak good words to people.
Then he said: Visit their sick, attend their funerals, testify for them and against them, pray with them in their mosques, and fulfill their rights.

Then he said: What is more severe upon a people who claim to follow a people and act upon their words, yet they order them and forbid them but do not accept from them, and they publicize their hadith among their enemies, so their enemies come to us and say to us: 'A certain group says and narrates such and such?'
We say: We disavow the one who says this, so the disavowal falls upon them.
ai.seo_question: What are the key social duties and signs of true followership according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the essential characteristics of the Shia community, emphasizing social humility and the fulfillment of communal duties like visiting the sick and praying in their mosques. He provides a critical criterion for authentic allegiance: those who claim to follow the Imams but disobey their commands while publicizing their teachings to enemies risk incurring the Imams' disavowal (al-Bara'ah). This highlights the link between practical obedience and preserving the community's reputation against external criticism.

en.badr-shahin: Mohammed bin Musa bin al-Mutawakkil, Allah may have mercy upon him, narrated from … Abdullah bin Sinan
that he heard Abu Abdullah (a) saying: O servants of Allah, I command you to cling to God-fearing.
Do not disregard people so that you will not be humiliated.
Allah, Powerful and Majestic is He, says in His Book: Speak righteous words to people.
( : ) He (a) then said: Visit the ailed people, participate in their funeral ceremonies, testify for and against them, offer prayer with them in their mosques, and fulfill their rights.

He (a) then said: Some people claim being our followers and acting upon our commandments, but they do not observe the matters of which we order them and do not stop committing the acts that we forbid. Moreover, they divulge our secrets before our enemies, who come to us for interrogating whether we had really said such things.
In such cases, we have to deny and disavow everyone who divulges such matters. Thus, our disavowal includes such people.
